title: Genuine Reformed imputation doctrine Rome dare not openly deny
source_text: XXIX. Haec est vera & germana Reformatorum doctrina de justificatione nostra per Christi Domini nostri justitiam nobis imputatam, quam ita manifestam reddit, tum fidei analogia, tum ipse communis Christianorum sensus, & interna conscientiae vox, ut nequidem Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae illi aperte contradicere audeant; sed quum simpliciter & nude proponitur, cogantur ei dare manus, & veritati illius subscribere.
pass_a_gloss: This is the true and genuine doctrine of the Reformers concerning our justification by our Lord Christ’s righteousness imputed to us, which the analogy of faith, the common sense of Christians, and the inward voice of conscience make so plain that not even the doctors of the Roman Church dare openly contradict it; but when it is simply and nakedly proposed, they are compelled to give it their hands and subscribe to its truth.
pass_b_english: Plain Reformed imputation is so clear that Rome dare not openly deny it when simply stated.
